children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange continued to rally Tuesday, following the lead of crude oil.

An analyst said the attack on a major pipeline in Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi rebels last weekend and its ensuing shutdown was the major driver behind crude oil prices, which gained nearly US$3 per barrel.
However, Chicago soyoil was down, Malaysian palm oil was up and European rapeseed was mixed.
Statistics Canada will release its latest principal field crop report Wednesday.
Northern and southern Alberta will see showers Tuesday, while central parts will be sunny. Daytime temperatures throughout the Prairies won't be any higher than 15 degrees Celsius.
The Canadian dollar was down less than one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared with Monday's close.
About 32,000 canola contracts have traded at 11:32 a.m. ET. Prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne:
